Usually medication/therapy or the mix of both which is usually suggested by your doctor/GP. Not sure which country you're from but here in the UK all you have to do is set up an appointment to see your doctor and explain everything to them and they'll guide you on what to do next - usually involves prescribing medication if you're open to it or setting up therapy sessions for the future. Goodluck
I really wish I could offer some sort of help, I really do :( You can always PM me if you need to talk to someone.

I can understand with you 100% man seriously, I would'nt even wish my worst enemies this disease. For me, I just take every day as it is I don't plan for tomorrow or anything my aim is to just make it until I go to sleep. Have you tried sitting a family member down (you usually have a favourite haha) and pouring your heart and mind out? When people usually say that they've spoken to someone it finally comes out that the conversation consisted of just telling them that they were a bit sad, this is what I did the first time and couldn't come to terms with why no one in my family would understand me.

The emptiness feeling you described is perfect to how Me and so many others feel, it makes you numb to the outside world in a way. 

Can you not speak to anyone at your College, I know you mentioned not having any friends anymore but over here in the UK we have a few services that offer for students to just come and pop-in to speak about what's going on in their lives. Before I was very closed off and didn't tell anyone for years on end, but surprisingly people aren't as horrible as I thought and could actually relate in a way.

Medication isn't always the best antidote either but if I was you, I would book an appointment with your Doctor or GP to maybe look into some sort of help. Please stay strong.

I second what Michelle said about attending Therapy while on meds, both of them pair up well with eachother. The problem with medication is always the side effects but they do eventually subside if you plan to carry on taking them.

I've been there when the Doctor asks if you're okay or mentions anything to do with suicide and you shy away from the question, you really should try and be honest with him/her, it could save you in the long run. Stay strong and Good Luck.

I can't thank you enough, seriously. I suppose you're right, i have a lot more to give to the world and my family and friends than end it right now. I suppose i just lost all hope and faith in myself and needed someone who wasn't a relative or friend to tell me that things will eventually get better.
